article_title: 'Interactive Online Learning Method for Students Based on Artificial Intelligence'
citation: Li C, Yin W. (2025). Interactive online learning method for students based on artificial intelligence. Discover Artificial Intelligence 5:201. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-025-00401-x
title: DMO-GRU hybrid framework: Dwarf Mongoose Optimization tuning of a Gated Recurrent Unit for student performance prediction
description: The DMO-GRU framework combines the Dwarf Mongoose Optimization algorithm with a Gated Recurrent Unit neural network. DMO performs feature selection and automatic hyperparameter tuning (learning rate, dropout, number of hidden units), while the GRU captures temporal patterns in student learning data. The article states that "our hybrid DMO-GRU model makes use of DMO's worldwide search capabilities" to improve GRU's learning process and produce more precise forecasts of student engagement and performance. The authors position the integration as suited to noisy, sparse or irregular educational data and as promoting individualized, adaptive learning.
requirements: Educational datasets with sequential student learning behaviour for the GRU to model
Hyperparameter search space for DMO to tune (learning rate, batch size, hidden units, dropout rate)
constraints: Evaluation relied on benchmark datasets with limited real-world testing, per the article's stated limitations
target_learning_goals: predicting student engagement and performance outcomes
examples: The model was implemented in MATLAB R2023a and compared against GRU, LSTM, CNN-GRU, Random Forest and XGBoost using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and training time (Table 2)
key_sources: Li C, Yin W. (2025). Interactive online learning method for students based on artificial intelligence. Discover Artificial Intelligence 5:201. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-025-00401-x

article_title: Stroop task performance across the lifespan: High cognitive reserve in older age is associated with enhanced proactive and reactive interference control
citation: Patrick D. Gajewski, Michael Falkenstein, Sven Th€ones, Edmund Wascher. (2020). Stroop task performance across the lifespan: High cognitive reserve in older age is associated with enhanced proactive and reactive interference control. NeuroImage 207 (2020) 116430. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2019.116430
title: Dual-mechanisms of cognitive control (DMC) framework applied to lifespan interference control
description: The dual-mechanisms of cognitive control framework by Braver (2012) distinguishes two modes of cognitive control. According to the article, "proactive control relies upon the anticipation and prevention of interference before it occurs, whereas reactive control relates to the detection and resolution of interference after its occurrence". The framework proposes that situational factors or individual strategy shift the weighting between the two modes, with situational factors inducing intra-individual variability and stable traits producing inter-individual differences. The study uses the CNV as an index of proactive control and the P2/N2 complex as a correlate of reactive control to locate performance differences between old performer groups within this framework.
requirements: Tasks with high control demands in which proactive and reactive control settings can be dissociated, e.g. cue-based Stroop blocks with preparatory intervals
constraints: The article notes cross-sectional studies are less useful to evaluate compensatory or gain processes
examples: The study mapped CNV amplitudes onto proactive control and target-locked P2/N2 amplitudes onto reactive control across three Stroop blocks of increasing difficulty
key_sources: Patrick D. Gajewski, Michael Falkenstein, Sven Th€ones, Edmund Wascher. (2020). Stroop task performance across the lifespan: High cognitive reserve in older age is associated with enhanced proactive and reactive interference control. NeuroImage 207 (2020) 116430. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2019.116430

article_title: COVID-19: A cross-national analysis with PISA data
citation: Giang Pham, Franziska Maria Locher, Dimitra Kolovou, Eliane Arnold. (2026). COVID-19: A cross-national analysis with PISA data. Learning and Instruction 105 (2026) 102366. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2026.102366
title: Dynamic Model of Educational Effectiveness as framework for pandemic-era teaching and learning conditions
description: The study draws on the Dynamic Model of Educational Effectiveness (DMEE; Creemers & Kyriakides, 2008), which "provides a general framework for exploring interactions among factors operating at four levels (student, teacher/classroom, school, and system/context)". The authors chose it because it emphasises the system level, which shaped pandemic schooling through measures such as closure duration, and because it has been used in cross-national PISA research. Pandemic-specific distance-learning elements were supplemented from related distance-education models.
requirements: Applicable when system-level policy factors (e.g. school-closure duration) are measured alongside classroom- and student-level conditions
constraints: The article notes new distance-learning elements gained importance during the pandemic that are not explicitly defined in the DMEE
target_learning_goals: Sustaining student performance in mathematics, reading, and science during irregular schooling
examples: The authors operationalised system-level conditions via school-closure and stringency indices and teacher/classroom and student conditions via the PISA 2022 Global Crises Module
key_sources: Giang Pham, Franziska Maria Locher, Dimitra Kolovou, Eliane Arnold. (2026). COVID-19: A cross-national analysis with PISA data. Learning and Instruction 105 (2026) 102366. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2026.102366

citation: Tacoma, S., Heeren, B., Jeuring, J., & Drijvers, P. (2020). Intelligent Feedback on Hypothesis Testing. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00218-y
title: Hypothesis-testing construction tasks in the Digital Mathematics Environment with ITS feedback
description: Six hypothesis-testing construction tasks delivered in the Digital Mathematics Environment, in which students freely select steps from a drop-down menu called "Action", complete them in answer boxes, and state an overall conclusion. Two versions existed: an experimental version with intelligent feedback on steps and logic, plus a hint button, and a control version providing only verification feedback on individual answer boxes. The domain module was built on the Ideas framework, expanded to support constraints, and its software is available at http://hackage.haskell.org/package/ideas-statistics. A pilot with five students informed improvements to feedback formulation and prioritization.
requirements: A domain module added to the Digital Mathematics Environment enabling intelligent feedback on hypothesis-testing construction tasks
constraints: Assessment criteria for correct solutions were stricter in the experimental condition, requiring four essential steps, than in the control condition, which required only a correct conclusion about the null hypothesis
target_learners: first-year psychology students at a Dutch university
target_learning_goals: proficiency in carrying out hypothesis tests
examples: In the final two tasks the test statistic was given, so fewer steps were needed for a complete solution than in earlier tasks
key_sources: Tacoma, S., Heeren, B., Jeuring, J., & Drijvers, P. (2020). Intelligent Feedback on Hypothesis Testing. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00218-y

article_title: Simulation-Based Learning Supported by Technology to Enhance Critical Thinking in Nursing Students: Scoping Review.
citation: Stenseth Hege Vistven et al. (2025). Simulation-Based Learning Supported by Technology to Enhance Critical Thinking in Nursing Students: Scoping Review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/58744
title: DeLone and McLean IS Success Model as an organizing framework for enablers and barriers of technology-supported SBL for critical thinking
description: The review used the DeLone and McLean model of information system success as a deductive lens to organize enablers and barriers identified inductively from included studies. The model "aims to evaluate the success of an IS and suggests that its dimensions are interrelated and influence each other." Dimensions include system quality, information quality, service quality, use and intention to use, satisfaction, and net benefits, each mapped to a theme such as affinity for technology, realism, accessibility, engagement and motivation, validation, return on investment, and enhanced critical thinking.
requirements: Themes were sorted into the model's predetermined categories through deductive analysis after inductive thematic analysis
constraints: The review notes its main findings on RQ 3 related primarily to the information quality and use and intention to use dimensions
key_sources: Stenseth Hege Vistven et al. (2025). Simulation-Based Learning Supported by Technology to Enhance Critical Thinking in Nursing Students: Scoping Review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/58744

article_title: The Effect of Discourse Markers Instruction on EFL Learners' Writing
citation: Nader Assadi Aidinlou & Hakimeh Shahrokhi mehr. (2012). The Effect of Discourse Markers Instruction on EFL Learners' Writing. World Journal of Education, Vol. 2, No. 2. http://dx.doi.org/10.5430/wje.v2n2p10
title: Discourse markers as cohesive devices classified into additive, adversative, causal and temporal conjunctive types
description: The article adopts Halliday and Hasan's account of conjunction as one of five cohesive devices, treating discourse markers as formal markers that "relate sentences, clauses and paragraphs to each other". Conjunctives are "divided into four general and major parts as "additive, adversative, causal, temporal"", and the article adds other types (e.g. actually, after all, in fact, such as). Unlike reference, substitution or ellipsis, conjunction signals how the writer wants the reader to relate upcoming text to prior text rather than directing the reader to search for missing information. The study's treatment taught frequently used markers from each family in authentic texts.
requirements: Instruction should focus on families of conjunctives or individual conjunctives that are frequently and extensively used in authentic reading texts
constraints: The article notes cohesion alone is not enough to make a text coherent, citing Thornbury (1997), and that DMs are by no means the only evidence for a well-organized cohesive text
target_learning_goals: Recognition and appropriate use of discourse markers
examples: Treatment examples included markers such as besides, moreover, similarly (additive); however, on the other hand, yet (adversative); therefore, thus (causal); first, then, finally (temporal)
key_sources: Nader Assadi Aidinlou & Hakimeh Shahrokhi mehr. (2012). The Effect of Discourse Markers Instruction on EFL Learners' Writing. World Journal of Education, Vol. 2, No. 2. http://dx.doi.org/10.5430/wje.v2n2p10

article_title: Expertise Related Changes in Resting-State Functional Connectivity Patterns Following a Clinical Reasoning and Decision-Making Task.
citation: Cortese, F., Hruska, P., McLaughlin, K. J., Coderre, S. P., Protzner, A. B., Krigolson, O. E., Hecker, K. G. (2026). Expertise Related Changes in Resting‐State Functional Connectivity Patterns Following a Clinical Reasoning and Decision‐Making Task. Brain and Behavior 16, no. 1: e71153. https://doi.org/10.1002/brb3.71153
title: Default mode network subsystem account of post-task expert–novice differences
description: The article reinterprets its connectivity findings through a contemporary fractionation of the default mode network into three interacting subsystems: a core (mPFC–PCC/precuneus) supporting self-referential integration, a medial temporal subsystem supporting episodic/semantic construction, and a dorsomedial subsystem supporting mentalizing. Functions are characterized as "cold" (memory construction, semantic integration, perspective taking) and "hot" (valuation/affect-laden appraisal in vmPFC and PCC). On this reading, novice FPPFC–PCC coupling post-task reflects engagement of cold core/medial-temporal subsystems, while experts show sustained coupling of frontoparietal control with evaluative/attentional circuits and reduced DMN reliance.
requirements: The account presupposes the post-task resting-state group differences measured with seed-based and PLS analyses of the right FPPFC seed; the article recommends longer resting-state durations (10 to 15 min) for more stable functional connectivity maps.
constraints: Derived as a reinterpretation of findings from a small sample (20 participants) of gastroenterologists and second-year medical students; the article notes small sample sizes can reduce statistical power and replicability, and the expert group was on average 13 years older than the novice group, with age incorporated as a nuisance variable.
target_learning_goals: Development of diagnostic clinical reasoning expertise
key_sources: Cortese, F., Hruska, P., McLaughlin, K. J., Coderre, S. P., Protzner, A. B., Krigolson, O. E., Hecker, K. G. (2026). Expertise Related Changes in Resting‐State Functional Connectivity Patterns Following a Clinical Reasoning and Decision‐Making Task. Brain and Behavior 16, no. 1: e71153. https://doi.org/10.1002/brb3.71153
